title: LYNTLAND Study: “Lymph Node Transfer for Lymphedema After Neck Dissection”: A Prospective, Multicenter Study on the Efficacy and Safety of Free Vascularized Lymph Node Transfer Following Neck Dissection
summary:
Head and neck tumors are often treated with surgery followed by radiation therapy. A possible long-term consequence of these treatments is lymphedema in the head and neck region, which results from damage to the lymphatic system. Those affected often suffer from swelling, difficulty swallowing and speaking, and a reduced quality of life.

Treatment to date has been predominantly conservative, involving manual lymphatic drainage and compression therapy. For persistent symptoms, only limited surgical treatment options have been available so far.

Free vascularized lymph node transfer (VLNT) is a microsurgical procedure that has already been used successfully for lymphedema in other parts of the body. However, there have been only isolated case reports regarding head and neck lymphedema to date. The aim of the planned study is therefore to investigate the efficacy and safety of this procedure and to assess potential improvements in lymphedema, function, and quality of life.

interventions.name:
Surgical Intervention Group:
Lymphovenous anastomosis (LVA) in patients with lymphedema in the head and neck region for whom curative therapy is no longer effective. A single surgical procedure with a 24-month follow-up period, during which subjective and objective data on the safety of the surgery

Control group without surgical intervention:
Patients with lymphedema in the head and neck region for whom curative therapy is no longer effective. Further curative therapy with a 24-month follow-up period, during which subjective and objective data on the safety of the surgery and quality of life

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Intervention group:
German-speaking
• Written informed consent following comprehensive counseling
• Histologically confirmed malignant disease in the head and neck region
• Post-operative status following unilateral or bilateral neck dissection as part of tumor therapy
• Clinically and/or instrumentally confirmed secondary head and neck lymphedema (external
and/or internal)
• Completion of all primary and adjuvant oncological therapies (surgery, radiation, and/
or chemotherapy)
• A minimum of six months since completion of tumor therapy
• No evidence of locoregional recurrence or distant metastasis as part of
routine tumor follow-up
• Persistent symptoms and/or functional limitations despite conservative
therapy
• Suitability for microsurgical intervention under general anesthesia
• Suitability for prospective assignment to the intervention group based on
the matching criteria defined in the study protocol.

Control group:
• Age ≥ 18 and ≤ 80 years
• German-speaking
• Written informed consent following comprehensive explanation regarding data collection and participation
in the study’s measurements
• Refusal of surgical therapy
• Other criteria as in the intervention group (histologically confirmed malignancy,
status following neck dissection, confirmed secondary head and neck lymphedema,
completed oncological therapy with a minimum interval of six months, no evidence of recurrence or
metastasis, persistent symptoms despite conservative therapy)
Exclusion criteria:
Intervention group:
• Active, recurrent, or metastatic cancer requiring current treatment
• Planned further oncological treatment at the time of study enrollment
• Ineligibility for surgery or contraindications to general anesthesia
• Contraindications to the intended donor site (e.g., prior surgeries,
vascular anomalies, or relevant comorbidities)
• Severe, uncontrolled internal medical comorbidities with increased surgical risk
• Acute local or systemic infections
• Pregnancy or breastfeeding
• Inability to give informed consent or to participate in follow-up examinations
• Anticipated lack of compliance with aftercare and follow-up
• MRI: Claustrophobia, contraindication to MRI imaging

Control group:
• Active, recurrent, or metastatic tumor disease requiring current treatment
• Planned further oncological therapy at the time of study enrollment
• Severe uncontrolled concomitant medical conditions
• Acute local or systemic infections
• Pregnancy or breastfeeding
• Inability to give informed consent or to participate in follow-up visits
• Anticipated lack of compliance with aftercare and
